reason: The value is below the +0.002 bar and below LB noise. (1) Node-multiplier check. The metric is adjusted = J*(1-0.1*(T_pred-T_true)/T_true), linear on both sides (tools/official/metrics.md l.41-49). The head cut the dummy-test nodes by 2.9% (exp51 vs exp48) and by 2.4% (x138 vs readmit-v1) (experiments/ext_x138/DIFF.md s.4). So about +0.0022..+0.0027 of x138's +0.007 is node multiplier, not localisation. Also, +0.007 is a single LB sample with ~0.003-0.004 noise, and on our base the same head gave only +0.002. Localisation value is therefore at most ~+0.004-0.005 per -0.16 um of mean GT distance. (2) What pass 2 can reach. The public head's all-peak mean shift is ~0 (-0.017/+0.117/+0.057 um; out_full_P/report.json). A second pass of the same head therefore cannot remove the embryo-convention residual bias (+0.45/+0.33/+0.42 um on 6bba, ~0 on 44b6; out_full_P.log emb rows), and gate (c) forbids that anyway. It can only shrink variance. By my Gaussian decomposition, the public residual sigma is ~0.89 um/axis on 6bba and ~0.81 on 44b6. A head retrained in-embryo (leak5 'new', optimistic because of 44b6 crop leakage) gets ~0.775. So even the full variance gap is about -13% of the bias-free distance, and only the 'undershoot' part of it can be recovered by re-applying an unchanged head at off-grid, out-of-distribution trilinear features. Per-axis MAE barely moved in pass 1 (z 1.11->1.08, y 0.63->0.57, x 0.58->0.60 worse). Most of pass 1's -9.5% is the median collapse from resolving z-plane ambiguity (1.72->1.35), a one-shot effect that iteration does not repeat. (3) Arithmetic. Gate (a) threshold -3% = -0.046 um -> ~+0.0012 at pass 1's marginal rate; the optimistic -5% -> ~+0.002. Diminishing returns apply because the tail gates are coarse (relink 7 um, readmit 4 um, gapfill 3.5 um). Times P(gate) 0.35, the expected public gain is ~+0.0005, and ~+0.001 conditional on shipping. (4) The probe cannot resolve it. Byte-identical notebooks scored 0.946/0.942, so one slot against #34 with 'tie allowed' adopts a null change about 50% of the time. The gate measures fixed-pair distance, not the metric: pass 1 even reduced the 7 um re-match count (132,366->132,326) while the LB rose. (5) Transfer. UNet features are in-sample on all 199 train videos, so they are sharper there than on hidden embryos. The information carried by off-grid trilinear reads is then overstated offline, which is pass-dependent optimism (not pass-independent, as the idea claims). 44b6's 20 gate clips are overlapping crops of one recording (fewer independent samples). Private gain is at best equal to public, likely smaller.
fix_if_any: A zero-GPU pre-gate before any capture2. On the existing leak5 captures (experiments/coordhead_retrain/captures on Vitalii's PC, CPU, minutes via a tools/train_coordhead.py-style eval), scale the public head output by s in {0.8,1.0,1.2,1.4,1.6}. Report fixed-pair mean, MAE per axis, m7 and share4 per embryo. If s_opt <= 1.1 or the gain at s_opt is < 3% on either embryo, the head is calibrated: pass 2 has nothing to recover, so kill it (the most likely outcome, since MAE barely moved in pass 1). Only if s_opt >= 1.25 with >= 4% on BOTH embryos is capture2 worth doing. Even then, replace the distance gate with a metric gate: run the x138 tail (edge net + ILP + flow relink/readmit/gapfill) on the 40 held-out train videos with and without pass 2, and require >= +0.003 adjusted-edge J on each embryo with node counts within 1%. Treat that lab number with the in-sample-edge-net discount (lab +0.0019 -> LB +0.001 for division insertion). Ship only as a rider on a submission that already carries a larger change, never as its own slot. Kill it if the gain is below the noise floor.
realistic_public_gain: +0.0005 expected (+0.001 if it passes the gate and ships; range -0.002 to +0.003); undetectable with one slot (noise ~0.003-0.004)
realistic_private_gain: +0.0003 expected (0 to +0.002 if shipped). It cannot fix the unknown convention offset of the hidden embryos, and the offline gain is optimistic because the UNet features are in-sample.
